# PlainArmor

> PlainArmor shows a company, on screen, how someone could fake an email from its domain, and walks it through the fix.

## Company

- [About PlainArmor](https://plainarmor.com/about): What PlainArmor does, who it is for, how the service works (public DNS only, nothing sent) and how to contact the team.

## Industries

- [Can someone email as your dental practice? Here is how to check](https://plainarmor.com/industries/dentists): Fake lab invoices and "new bank details" emails can look like they come from your practice. See how to stop your domain being spoofed.
- [General contractors: fake draw requests and invoices that look like yours](https://plainarmor.com/industries/general-contractors): Fake progress-payment invoices and "new account" emails can use your company name. See the plain-English domain fix for contractors.

- [Insurance agencies: protect the sender name your clients trust](https://plainarmor.com/industries/insurance-agencies): Fake premium and claim-payment emails can use your agency's name. See what closes the gap at the domain level, in plain English.

- [Marketing agencies and IT providers: your domain is a key to your clients](https://plainarmor.com/industries/agencies-it-services): Marketing agencies and IT providers are trusted by clients. See how a fake email from your domain could do harm and how to close the gap.

## Blog

- [What to ask your IT contractor about email security](https://plainarmor.com/blog/questions-to-ask-it-contractor-email-security): A list of plain questions for your IT provider about SPF, DKIM, DMARC, account security and incident response, with what a good answer sounds like.
- [What to do if a customer got a fake email from you](https://plainarmor.com/blog/customer-got-fake-email-from-you): Step-by-step response when a customer or vendor reports a scam email that appears to come from your business, plus how to prevent a repeat.
- [Business email compromise (BEC): what small businesses need to know](https://plainarmor.com/blog/business-email-compromise-small-business): BEC is fraud that tricks staff into sending money or data by posing as someone they trust. Learn the common types and simple ways to reduce risk.
- [Can someone send email as my domain?](https://plainarmor.com/blog/can-someone-send-email-as-my-domain): Yes, if your domain has no enforced DMARC policy, a stranger can often send mail that looks like it is from you. Here is how to check and what to do.
- [CEO and boss impersonation emails: how to spot and stop them](https://plainarmor.com/blog/ceo-impersonation-emails): Scammers pose as the owner or boss to push staff into quick payments or gift-card buys. Learn the patterns and a few rules that defuse them.
- [Cyber insurance and email authentication: what small businesses should know](https://plainarmor.com/blog/cyber-insurance-and-email-authentication): Insurers sometimes ask about email security controls. We explain what to check on your application and why to confirm details with your own agent.
- [DIY, paid DMARC monitoring, or step-by-step instructions: how to choose](https://plainarmor.com/blog/diy-vs-paid-monitoring-vs-instructions): Three ways to fix DMARC: figure it out yourself, pay for ongoing monitoring, or follow step-by-step instructions. Fair pros, cons and who each suits.
- [What to do when DMARC breaks your invoices or newsletters](https://plainarmor.com/blog/dmarc-broke-invoices-newsletters): If legitimate email is bouncing or hitting spam after a DMARC change, here is how to diagnose which sender failed, fix it, and avoid repeating it.
- [DMARC policies explained: none, quarantine, reject](https://plainarmor.com/blog/dmarc-policies-none-quarantine-reject): The three DMARC policies tell receivers what to do with mail that fails checks. Learn what each means, the risks of each, and when to use them.
- [Email authentication and deliverability: what is the connection?](https://plainarmor.com/blog/email-authentication-and-deliverability): SPF, DKIM and DMARC help legitimate email reach inboxes, but they are not the only factor. What authentication does and does not do for delivery.
- [An email authentication checklist for small businesses](https://plainarmor.com/blog/email-authentication-checklist-small-business): A practical checklist covering SPF, DKIM, DMARC, sender inventory, account security and payment habits, in the order a small business should tackle them.
- [Fake invoice and bank-detail-change scams: how they work and how to stop them](https://plainarmor.com/blog/fake-invoice-bank-change-scams): How fake invoices and "we changed banks" emails work, the warning signs, and a simple payment-verification routine any small business can adopt today.
- [Google, Yahoo and Microsoft email sender requirements: what small businesses need to know](https://plainarmor.com/blog/google-yahoo-microsoft-sender-requirements): Gmail and Yahoo set sender rules from February 2024; Microsoft announced Outlook.com rules for high-volume senders. What they mean for small business.
- [How long does it take to fix DMARC?](https://plainarmor.com/blog/how-long-does-fixing-dmarc-take): The DNS edits take minutes, but safely reaching enforcement usually takes weeks. Here is a realistic, staged timeline and what makes it shorter or longer.
- [How to add a DMARC record at GoDaddy, Cloudflare, Namecheap, or any DNS host](https://plainarmor.com/blog/add-dmarc-record-godaddy-cloudflare-namecheap): The same four fields work at GoDaddy, Cloudflare, Namecheap and most DNS hosts. Here is what to enter, common mistakes, and how to confirm it worked.
- [How to check if your domain can be spoofed](https://plainarmor.com/blog/how-to-check-if-your-domain-can-be-spoofed): A plain-English walk-through for checking your DMARC, SPF and DKIM settings and deciding whether someone could send email that looks like it is from you.
- [How to find out who sends email as your domain](https://plainarmor.com/blog/find-who-sends-email-as-your-domain): Before you enforce DMARC, list every tool that sends mail as you: invoices, newsletters, forms, CRMs. Here is a practical way to find them all.
- [How to move DMARC from monitor to enforcement safely](https://plainarmor.com/blog/move-dmarc-from-monitor-to-enforcement): A staged plan for going from p=none to quarantine to reject without blocking your own invoices, newsletters, or customer mail.
- [How to read your DMARC record](https://plainarmor.com/blog/how-to-read-your-dmarc-record): A DMARC record is a short line of text. This guide explains each part (v, p, rua, pct, sp, adkim, aspf) in plain English with working examples.
- [How to set up SPF for Google Workspace](https://plainarmor.com/blog/set-up-spf-google-workspace): The SPF record for Google Workspace is one line. Learn what it means, how to add other senders safely, and the mistakes that make SPF fail.
- [How to set up SPF for Microsoft 365](https://plainarmor.com/blog/set-up-spf-microsoft-365): The Microsoft 365 SPF record is one line. Learn what it says, how to add other senders without breaking it, and how to confirm it is working.
- [How to turn on DKIM in Google Workspace](https://plainarmor.com/blog/turn-on-dkim-google-workspace): DKIM adds a signature to your outgoing mail so receivers can verify it. Here is how to generate the key, publish it, and start signing in Google Workspace.
- [How to turn on DKIM in Microsoft 365](https://plainarmor.com/blog/turn-on-dkim-microsoft-365): Microsoft 365 uses two CNAME records for DKIM. Here is where to find the values, how to publish them, and how to switch signing on and verify it.
- [Is DMARC worth it for a 5-person company?](https://plainarmor.com/blog/is-dmarc-worth-it-for-small-business): A fair look at what DMARC costs a small team in time and risk, what it protects, what it does not, and when it makes sense to do it.
- [Lookalike domains vs. spoofed domains](https://plainarmor.com/blog/lookalike-domains-vs-spoofed-domains): A spoofed domain fakes your exact address. A lookalike domain is a different address that resembles yours. They need different defenses. Here is how.
- [SPF vs DKIM vs DMARC: the plain-English difference](https://plainarmor.com/blog/spf-vs-dkim-vs-dmarc): SPF lists who may send, DKIM signs messages, DMARC sets the rule and reports. Here is how the three fit together, in plain English with an analogy.
- [DMARC alignment explained](https://plainarmor.com/blog/dmarc-alignment-explained): Alignment means the domain that passed SPF or DKIM matches the From address people see. It is why third-party senders often fail DMARC. Explained simply.
- [What DMARC does not protect against](https://plainarmor.com/blog/what-dmarc-does-not-protect-against): DMARC blocks fakes of your exact domain, but not lookalike domains, hacked mailboxes, or scams sent to you. Here are the limits and what covers each gap.
- [What does DMARC p=none mean?](https://plainarmor.com/blog/dmarc-p-none-meaning): p=none is a monitoring setting. It gets you reports but asks receivers to take no action on fakes. Here is when it is useful and how to move past it.
- [What is BIMI, and does a small business need it?](https://plainarmor.com/blog/what-is-bimi): BIMI shows your verified logo beside your email in some inboxes. It needs strong DMARC and usually a paid certificate. Most small firms can skip it.
- [What is email spoofing, in plain English?](https://plainarmor.com/blog/what-is-email-spoofing): Email spoofing means sending a message that appears to come from someone else's address. Here is how it works and what small businesses can do about it.
- [Why your email looks real when it is fake](https://plainarmor.com/blog/why-fake-email-looks-real): A fake email can show the right name, address and logo because email has no built-in identity check. Here is what is behind the screen and how to look.

## Glossary

- [What Is Account Takeover?](https://plainarmor.com/glossary/account-takeover): Account takeover is when someone else gains access to a real email account. Why DMARC does not prevent it and how small businesses reduce the risk.
- [What Is BIMI?](https://plainarmor.com/glossary/bimi): BIMI lets a business display its logo next to authenticated email in supporting inboxes. How it relates to DMARC and whether you need it.
- [What Is a Bulk Sender?](https://plainarmor.com/glossary/bulk-sender): A bulk sender sends large volumes of email, such as newsletters or notices. Why mail providers expect authentication and what small businesses should do.
- [What Is Business Email Compromise (BEC)?](https://plainarmor.com/glossary/business-email-compromise): Business email compromise (BEC) is fraud where someone poses as a trusted contact by email to redirect money or data. Meaning and what to do.
- [What Is Display-Name Spoofing?](https://plainarmor.com/glossary/display-name-spoofing): Display-name spoofing shows a trusted person's name on an email sent from an unrelated address. Why DMARC cannot stop it and what to do.
- [What Is a DKIM Selector?](https://plainarmor.com/glossary/dkim-selector): A DKIM selector is the name that identifies which DKIM key to use for a message, so one domain can have several. What it means in practice.
- [What Is DKIM (DomainKeys Identified Mail)?](https://plainarmor.com/glossary/dkim): DKIM (DomainKeys Identified Mail) adds a digital signature to outgoing email, checked via a public key in DNS. Meaning for a small business.
- [What Is DMARC Alignment?](https://plainarmor.com/glossary/alignment): Alignment means the domain verified by SPF or DKIM matches the From address people see. Why DMARC needs it and what a small business should do.
- [What Is DMARC Enforcement?](https://plainarmor.com/glossary/enforcement): DMARC enforcement means your policy is quarantine or reject, so receivers act on failing mail. What it means and how to reach it safely.
- [What Does DMARC p=none Mean?](https://plainarmor.com/glossary/p-none): p=none is the DMARC monitoring setting that asks receivers to take no action on failing mail. What it means and why it is not enough alone.
- [What Does DMARC p=quarantine Mean?](https://plainarmor.com/glossary/p-quarantine): p=quarantine asks receivers to treat mail that fails DMARC as suspicious, often sending it to spam. What it means for a small business.
- [What Does DMARC p=reject Mean?](https://plainarmor.com/glossary/p-reject): p=reject is the strictest DMARC setting, asking receivers to refuse mail that fails checks. What it means and what can go wrong if senders are missing.
- [What Is the DMARC pct Tag?](https://plainarmor.com/glossary/pct-tag): The DMARC pct tag applies your policy to only a share of failing mail, so you can phase in enforcement. What it means and how to use it.
- [What Is a DMARC Policy?](https://plainarmor.com/glossary/dmarc-policy): A DMARC policy is the p= setting that tells receivers to take no action, quarantine or reject mail that fails checks. Meaning and what to do.
- [What Is a DMARC Report Service?](https://plainarmor.com/glossary/dmarc-report-service): A DMARC report service collects and turns raw DMARC reports into readable summaries of who sends email as your domain. When it helps.
- [What Are DMARC rua Reports?](https://plainarmor.com/glossary/rua-reports): rua reports are DMARC aggregate reports that mail providers send showing who uses your domain to send email. What they mean for a small business.
- [What Are DMARC ruf Reports?](https://plainarmor.com/glossary/ruf-reports): ruf reports are DMARC failure reports about individual messages that failed checks. What they are and whether a small business needs them.
- [What Is a DMARC Subdomain Policy?](https://plainarmor.com/glossary/subdomain-policy): The DMARC subdomain policy (sp tag) sets how receivers treat mail from subdomains of your domain. What it means and what to do.
- [What Is DMARC?](https://plainarmor.com/glossary/dmarc): DMARC is a DNS record that tells receivers what to do with email that fails SPF and DKIM checks for your domain. Meaning for a small business.
- [What Is a DNS Host?](https://plainarmor.com/glossary/dns-host): A DNS host is the service that holds and serves your domain's DNS records. How to find yours and why it matters for email security changes.
- [What Is DNS?](https://plainarmor.com/glossary/dns): DNS is the internet's address book that connects domain names to services such as websites and email. What it means for a small business.
- [What Is a Domain Registrar?](https://plainarmor.com/glossary/registrar): A registrar is the company where a domain name is registered and renewed. How it relates to your DNS host and why it matters for email.
- [What Is Email Authentication?](https://plainarmor.com/glossary/email-authentication): Email authentication is the set of checks, SPF, DKIM and DMARC, that help receivers verify who really sent a message. Meaning for small businesses.
- [What Is Email Deliverability?](https://plainarmor.com/glossary/deliverability): Deliverability is how likely your email is to reach the inbox instead of spam or being rejected. How authentication and DMARC relate to it.
- [How Does Email Forwarding Affect DMARC?](https://plainarmor.com/glossary/forwarding-and-dmarc): Forwarded email can fail SPF because it comes from a new server. How forwarding interacts with DMARC and what a small business can do.
- [What Is an Email Gateway?](https://plainarmor.com/glossary/email-gateway): An email gateway filters incoming and sometimes outgoing mail for spam and threats. How it differs from DMARC and whether a small business needs one.
- [What Is an Email Header?](https://plainarmor.com/glossary/email-header): An email header is the hidden technical information attached to every message, showing its path and authentication results. How to use it.
- [What Is Email Spoofing?](https://plainarmor.com/glossary/spoofing): Email spoofing is faking the sender of a message so it appears to come from someone else. What it means for a small business and what to do.
- [From Address vs Return-Path: What Is the Difference?](https://plainarmor.com/glossary/from-address-vs-return-path): The From address is what people see; the Return-Path is a hidden bounce address SPF checks. Why the difference matters for spoofing and DMARC.
- [What Is a Lookalike Domain?](https://plainarmor.com/glossary/lookalike-domain): A lookalike domain is a different web address that closely resembles yours. Why DMARC cannot stop it and what a small business can do instead.
- [What Is a Mail Provider?](https://plainarmor.com/glossary/mail-provider): A mail provider is the service that hosts your business mailboxes and sends your email. Why it matters when setting up email protection.
- [What Is MTA-STS?](https://plainarmor.com/glossary/mta-sts): MTA-STS tells other mail servers to use encrypted connections when delivering mail to your domain. How it differs from DMARC.
- [What Is an MX Record?](https://plainarmor.com/glossary/mx-record): An MX record is a DNS entry that says which servers receive email for your domain. What it does and does not do for email security.
- [What Is Phishing?](https://plainarmor.com/glossary/phishing): Phishing is a message that tricks someone into giving up money, passwords or information. What it means for a small business and what to do.
- [What Is Spear Phishing?](https://plainarmor.com/glossary/spear-phishing): Spear phishing is a targeted phishing message tailored to a specific person or company. What it means for a small business and what to do.
- [What Is the SPF Lookup Limit?](https://plainarmor.com/glossary/spf-lookup-limit): SPF allows at most 10 DNS lookups per check. Why exceeding it breaks SPF and what a small business should do about it.
- [SPF Softfail vs Hardfail: What Is the Difference?](https://plainarmor.com/glossary/spf-softfail-vs-hardfail): SPF softfail (~all) is a weak warning and hardfail (-all) says unauthorized servers are not allowed. What the difference means for your domain.
- [What Is SPF (Sender Policy Framework)?](https://plainarmor.com/glossary/spf): SPF (Sender Policy Framework) is a DNS record listing which servers may send email for your domain. What it means for a small business.
- [What Is a Third-Party Sender?](https://plainarmor.com/glossary/third-party-sender): A third-party sender is an outside service that sends email as your domain, such as billing or marketing tools. Why it matters for DMARC.
- [What Is a TXT Record?](https://plainarmor.com/glossary/txt-record): A TXT record is a DNS entry that holds text, used to publish SPF, DKIM and DMARC settings. What it means for a small business.
